title.narrative: Reports and Recommendations of the President

description.narrative: Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Enabling environment strengthened Indicator: At least 10 trained staff members from the MICTTD and the MISE (at least 30% women) demonstrated increased knowledge in resilient maritime infrastructure and causeways Progress/Status: The Mentoring Firm contract was signed in March 2024, and mobilization of staff to Kiribati has commenced in June 2024.
Significant capacity-building achievements include the establishment of a new Hydrographic Unit within the MICT Marine Division. Three new technical positions have been filled, and the staff have been trained to international standards, enabling them to independently conduct Multibeam Echo Sounder (MBES) surveys and submit data for chart updates. The Mentoring Firm and MISE have successfully completed the initial survey of all the causeways on Tabiteuea South. Data Source: Project progress reports Actual value:

Output: Enabling environment strengthened Indicator: At least 2 priority maritime projects identified Progress/Status: Consultant has been engaged to identify priority maritime projects. Feasibility study ongoing. Data Source: Project progress reports Actual value:

Output: Enabling environment strengthened Indicator: At least 5 mentored MISE staff members (at least 20% women) demonstrated improved skills in designing and maintaining disaster-resilient infrastructure built under the project Progress/Status: The Mentoring Firm contract was signed in March 2024, and mobilization of staff to Kiribati has commenced in June 2024.
A range of survey equipment has been provided to support its operations, and three technical positions (Safeguards Officer, GIS Officer, and Materials Engineer) have been successfully filled. However, three of the six newly approved technical positions (Project Officer, Assistant Civil Structural Engineer, and Laboratory Technician) have faced recruitment challenges. Despite multiple rounds of advertisement, no suitable candidates have been identified. MISE will reassess its staffing needs for the remaining positions once a decision is made on whether to convert the delivery modality of the causeways (under the WB-only financing component) from MISE force account to outsourcing. Data Source: Project progress reports Actual value:

Output: Resilience of outer island access infrastructure improved Indicator: 30 new ATONs installed Progress/Status: The design-build contract was signed in September 2024, with the World Bank approving $10 million additional financing for the contract shortfall. Detailed designs for outer island access infrastructure, including Aids to Navigation, are being completed by Hall Contracting Pty Ltd. (Australia, design-build contractor), pending final approval for dredging works in Beru. The construction supervision consultant, Sellhorn Ingenieurgesellschaft mbH (Germany), will validate the design. Civil works are expected to be completed by March 2027 as planned. Data Source: MICTTD annual reports Actual value:

Output: Safety of interisland navigation improved Indicator: 4 nautical charts on access routes to the project islands prepared Progress/Status: Hydrographic survey activities, conducted by IIC Technologies (NZ, consultant/surveyor), were successfully completed, and the United Kingdom Hydrographic Office (UK, quality control consultant) reviewed and validated all datasets for the four selected outer islands in May 2025. All charts are complete. The physical copies have been handed over to two MICT staff currently attending hydrographic data processing training at the UKHO in the UK. They are scheduled to return to Kiribati by end-January 2026, with the printed charts and the full survey dataset. As all objectives have been met, the UKHO contract will conclude as planned in February 2026, without the need for extension. Data Source: MICTTD annual reports Actual value:

Output: Enabling environment strengthened Indicator: 1 all-women routine maintenance team for causeways and maritime facilities pilot-tested Progress/Status: OIIU will undertake further consultations with women on project islands to define the scope of this activity. Data Source: Project progress reports Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: Not applicable Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: Not applicable Target year: 2026 Target value: 1

Output: Enabling environment strengthened Indicator: GBV framework prepared and 4 training sessions on handling GBV cases provided to all project staff members from the MISE and the MICTTD Progress/Status: The GBV Action Framework outlines mitigation and response measures for GBV and sexual exploitation, abuse, and harassment (SEAH). A dedicated phone line and email address have been established to report any GBV issues associated with KOITIIP, and awareness raising signs will be set up at work sites. Training in the GBV Action Framework, inductions to the Code of Conduct, and refreshers have been completed for the implementing entities and consultants engaged in the project. The design and build contract project workers will also undertake the same procedures. Data Source: Project progress reports Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: NA; 0 Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: NA; 0 Target year: 2026 Target value: 1; 4

Output: Resilience of outer island access infrastructure improved Indicator: 1 jetty, 4 boat ramps and 2 shelters, and 2 multipurpose maritime facilities designed with features that are friendly to older people, women, children, and people with disability Progress/Status: The design-build contract was signed in September 2024, with the World Bank approving $10 million additional financing for the contract shortfall. Detailed designs for outer island access infrastructure, including Aids to Navigation, have been completed by Hall Contracting Pty Ltd. (Australia, design-build contractor), except for the dredging works in Beru. The construction supervision consultant, Sellhorn Ingenieurgesellschaft mbH (Germany), will validate the design. Civil works are expected to be completed by March 2027 as planned. Data Source: MICTTD annual reports Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: 0 Target year: 2026 Target value: Y
Safety and resilience of transport connectivity in Abaiang, Beru, Nonouti, and Tabiteuea South improved

24-hour safe and resilient maritime navigation in 4 outer islands guided by nautical charts and maritime infrastructure provided Progress/Status: Contract with UKHO for hydrographic surveying was signed on 2 Dec 2020 (ADB USD523,336.78). Lidar data for the four outer islands (Abaiang, Beru, Nonouti, and Tabiteuea) have been completed. Survey results have been validated in May 2025. All charts are complete. The physical copies have been handed over to two MICT staff currently attending hydrographic data processing training at the UKHO in the UK. They are scheduled to return to Kiribati by 31 January 2026, with the printed charts and the full survey dataset. As all objectives have been met, the UKHO contract will conclude as planned in February 2026, without the need for extension.
Mobilization of the Mentoring Firm has commenced in June 2024. The Mentoring Firm: (a) supports MICT with quality control, detailed design review and supervision of maritime infrastructure being built under the Design-Build Contract; and (b) supports MISE with planning, designing, managing, executing, and supervising causeway rehabilitation. With the support of an engineer consultant, the contract for the Design-Build assignment was signed on 23 September 2024. Design work has commenced in November 2024 and is complete for all locations except for the dredging in Beru. Civil works are expected to be completed by April 2027
There are no overdue financial reports. The audited financial statements for the period ending 31 December 2024 were received on 29 June 2025. The FY24 Annual Work Plan and Budget has been cleared and is being closely monitored. The project contract and fixed asset register are well-maintained and updated regularly.
As of now, no need for further extension of grant closing date (currently on 31 December 2027) Data Source: MICTTD annual reports and project completion report Target value: Y Actual value:
